strings.name: Albert Bourla
strings.summary: Trained in veterinary medicine and reproductive biotechnology in Thessaloniki, Bourla joined Pfizer in 1993 and later led animal health, vaccines and innovative medicines. He became CEO in 2019, overseeing collaboration with BioNTech on a COVID-19 vaccine and acquisitions expanding cancer and obesity research. The vaccine was a cross-company and scientific team achievement; drug prices and research returns also test his management.

strings.highlights.h2.title: Expanding cancer treatment
strings.highlights.h2.text: Completed Seagen acquisition, adding antibody-drug conjugates to the business.

strings.timeline.t3.title: Vaccine received emergency authorization

strings.timeline.t5.title: Became CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Took charge of Pfizer, focusing its business on drug research.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became chief operating officer
strings.timeline.t6.text: Coordinated group research, manufacturing and commercial operations.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Pfizer
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began his corporate career in a technical animal-health role in Greece.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Thessaloniki
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Greece and later trained in veterinary medicine.
strings.timeline.t9.title: UK industry advertising-code ruling
strings.timeline.t9.text: Pfizer breached parts of the industry code over his child-vaccination interview; appeal overturned some more serious findings.
